_doc: A proposal for the owner, not a decision. Nothing here is loaded or built; every number is a starting value for the soak, and no node changes what a move is (same_answer_gate.identity_test; each node's verdict is its identity field).

elements.<el>.branches[].nodes[]: id, name, kind (enhance, variation, mastery, new_skill, passive, synergy, skill_set, world_only: the ids the loader and the page key on; the player reads kind_labels), chip (the BendStrip chip it sits under: LMB, E, 1-5, passive), extends_move (always a moves.json move id: the move the node sits under; for passives, sets and synergies only an anchor) and mode (its mode, '' when it is not one mode's), applies_to (passives, sets and synergies: what they change, as move/mode tags, passive:<id>, zone:<kind>, pool:grate, clash:stone or reaction:<id>; the loader validates these, not extends_move), grown (the Fireball), extends_passive (a passive's id), set (its skill set), home_ground (a set's home-ground passive), slot (a new skill's empty tap twice), requires (nodes that must be worn with it, ring and world), excludes (nodes it can't be worn with: the opposite pulls the loader recomputes from changes[]), ring_cost (its cost in points, ring and open world), ring_legal (false: open world only, or held), ring_note (why a number swap is open world only), held ({question, why}: held for the owner's answer, never worn until he says yes), world_gate (how the open world teaches it), effect, plus, minus, help (one line, 64 characters at most), answer (how he answers it), identity (its verdict under the identity test), changes, visual.

changes[]: {path, from, to} with path 'spec:<move>/<mode>.<field>' (moves.json moves[move].bend[mode]), 'move:<move>.<field>' (moves.json moves[move]), 'rules:<block>.<field>' (moves.json guard_rules, passives, lock, air_rules), 'stock:<field>' (rules.json stock; a guard's numbers reach the % ring only this way, as the wearer's own copy: RingRules reads stock guard_perfect_s and guard_catch_s (guard_outcome) and late_mult (the late hit), never the guard spec), 'class:<tag>.<field>' (rules.json stock.classes; a tag with '+' is the node's own variation tag copied from base_tag), 'set:<set>.<field>' (this file's skill_sets), or 'new:<what>' (a number in code today). 'new' records behaviour that needs code (what, where). Every change applies to the wearer only: nothing writes the shared data. from is today's value (checked against the files when this draft was made); new_field marks a per-move field that does not exist yet (from_path names the shared value it starts from); step marks an integer count moved by one; ring_only marks a ring number the open world doesn't take; note narrows when a change applies.

world_gate entries: practised:<move> (8 uses), expert:<move> (30 uses), expert_any:<element or set>:<n>, teacher:<element> (teacher:fire.storm for the Storm branch), set_teacher:<set>, trial:<id> (a short quest drill), quest:<set>, seen:<synergy id> (discovered by seeing the reaction once), story (as today), owner:answer (held: the owner's yes first), or a node id that must be learned first. Uses are counted per move id, as SwayCaster does today.

visual: kind (see visual_kinds), look (what to see), fx (Spellbreak references by index and name in artifacts/spellbreak_fx/specs/index.json, checked against bending_fx_map.json reviewer_rejections; sweep_flags = check it first), to_author (a gap to make).

fixed_skeleton: Which move sits on each key, the jab, the guard and each passive's rule never change. 1 is always Spike, Lash, Punch or Slice; E is always the element's guard. New skills only fill a tap twice that is empty today (earth, water and air key 4; fire key 5, since 4 already holds Breath); nothing is replaced, so Column, Geyser, High Kick and Mend stay. Every true string stays true (Column then Pebbles, Geyser then Lash or Spear, Kick or High Kick then Punch, Embers then Punch, Pull then Palm, Gust then Slice, and every jab, jab, Pop): a node that touches a string's lead or follow-up is re-checked before ranked (ring.string_recheck). Only key 4 makes walls (round-2 spec 2.7, rules.json _max_walls).

same_answer_gate.rule: A node may change what a move does after it lands, and its numbers; it never changes how the move is answered.
never_changes: its lane (along the floor, through the air, up from under you)
the guard that takes it and what that guard does with it
the wall cell that stops it (what each wall stops, is weak to and lets through)
its wind-up pose and limb (a twist may swap the release clip within the same limb)
its tell: the Column and Geyser 0.35 s rise, Lightning's 0.25 s hand flash, the Spike's raise at 60% of the lock, the Kick's crest that a jump clears
same_answer_gate.numbers: An enhance or passive changes each number by 20% at most, and always pairs a plus with a stated minus (integer counts move by one step). A twist may swap in an existing mode spec or its own % ring class, inside the identity test.
same_answer_gate.stacking: Two nodes changing one number the same way multiply their ratios (0.8 s x 0.95/0.8 x 0.7/0.8). Two nodes that pull one number opposite ways can't be worn together: the loader computes this from changes[] (a class change counts on its base tag), so a pick's cost is never bought back by another pick. A set twist's number is final for that move.
same_answer_gate.test: One test per node pins it: lane, guard outcome, wall outcome, tell timing, and that no node writes a victim's move speed, aim, camera, lock or guard. Every guard node also gets a % ring test: its perfect, late and catch outcomes through RingRules.guard_outcome with the wearer's own stock numbers, tapped and held.

identity_test.rule: Every node passes all five checks, or it is held for the owner or rescoped; each node's verdict is its identity field.
checks: Delivery: what the move sends keeps its count and shape until it lands or hits (one bolt stays one bolt, a spray a spray, a cone a cone, one rise one rise); what it leaves where it stops may be new (a burst, a puddle, a cloud, a seam, loose stones).
Lane: along the floor, through the air, or up from under you, as today.
KO role: a KO move stays a KO move (it may KO sooner or later), a launcher stays a launcher, a move that never KOs never does; every true string it leads or follows stays true (re-checked).

The key's job: LMB a close poke, 1 a shot, 2 a push or a launcher, 3 travel that never hits on its own path (it may leave matter behind, as Skate leaves puddles), 4 cover or placed ground, 5 recovery, E the guard table.

The answer: the guard that takes it and what that guard does, the wall cell that stops it, its tell, its pose and limb, its flight sound. A node may add an answer (a set's counters, a heated stone a Parry can send back), never remove or change one.
identity_test.applied: Held under it: Forked Fissure, Twin Geyser, Twin Wave and Twin Slice (a volley in place of one move), Surfacing Stomp, Breaker and Gust Step (a dash that hits), Reel (a KO strike made a pull that never KOs). lock_contract: Lock time stays the only spam limiter: no cooldown timers anywhere in the tree.
Every new skill has a lock_s; 'one at a time' (a new zone ends your old one) is a cap, not a timer.
A zone that covers its own caster (Shell and Bubble, both held) lasts no longer than its own lock and lets no lock start while it stands: what one lock buys is capped, and no timer is added.

Lock changes are the caster's own: techniques (kind mastery) and passives may start a lock part-full or fill it faster, never a zero lock and never a follow-up with no lock; enhances and twists never do.
Nothing in the tree adds lock time to, or sets back, the one who was hit; matter ticks and live reactions don't even do today's hit set-back.

tick_contract.rule: Matter ticks (gas, magma, burn lines, cold) add % only.
tick_contract.stacking: A body gains at most one tick each 0.5 s from matter, however many zones it stands in.
tick_contract.own_matter: Your own matter never hurts you; a reaction (a burst, live water or gas) hurts everyone in it.
tick_contract.how: Each tick is a no_flinch class (today's flag, as fire_wall/tick) plus the new no_hurt flag; the live reactions (Live Gas, Forked Lightning's live water) take no_hurt too.
tick_contract.open: Today Fire Wall's own tick (fire_wall/tick) does break a Lightning charge through BendR3.deliver; whether it should follow the same contract is an owner call.

universal_line: Fire lights gas; lightning charges it. Water washes gas and cools magma. Wind carries gas and snow. Mud stops floor fire. Fire melts frost.
reaction_rules: World rules act only on matter a pick makes (gas, mud, seams, crust, snow, dust), so Classic (no picks) plays exactly as today; a reaction that touches today's matter (steam, smoke, puddles, grates, fire walls) needs a node (Forked Lightning, Steamcraft, Scald, Frostwind).
A reaction has a fixed % that never stacks (two bursts in one spot are two separate hits, each owned).
Whoever sets a reaction off owns it: its % and its KO credit. A moved cloud belongs to the mover.

Terrain made from someone's matter stays his: a melted crust's puddle is the water's owner's (a grate's goes back to the grate); an obsidian stone counts toward the seam owner's three loose stones; the extra Avalanche stones that drop at a catcher's feet are the thrower's loose stones.
A reaction stales as the move that set it off.
Allies stay immune, as today (BendStatus never lets a bend reach the caster's allies).
Reactions are announced only at the existing callout spot (for example IGNITED!, OBSIDIAN!) with their own sound; nothing is drawn on anyone.

proposed_classes._about: Proposed % ring classes (rules.json stock.classes) for the new matter ticks and reactions. Variation tags are the base tag + '+' + a short name (copied from the base class, then changed as the node says). Every consumer of a tag (stale moves, rules.json stock.range.exempt, air_rules.lag_class, stock.return_base_tag, the highlights, bend_ai.json pct.strings) reads it through one shared lookup that strips the '+' part, with a test, so Short Fuse's Lightning keeps its range exemption and a bot's string table still matches a varied lead. no_flinch is today's flag (% only: no knock, no stun); no_hurt is new: the hit skips SwayCaster's hurt handling (no lock set-back, no Lightning-charge break: BendR3.deliver calls took_hit on every hit today), adds no string hit or decay, and never counts toward stale moves.

ring.everything_open: Every ring-legal node is open to everyone in the ring and in every PvP mode, whatever they have learned in the open world.

ring.tier: Everyone casts at practice tier 1.0. The % ring already reads every lock at its moves.json time (SwayCaster.tier_mult returns 1.0 under round 3); the classic zones ring needs the same gate once free_use goes off, or open-world practice would shorten its locks.
ring.numbers: Each node's ring numbers are its own (they never read open-world ranks II and III).
ring.visibility: Both loadouts on the versus card before the countdown (one line each) and in F1 and Esc at any time; a counter card gives one 'how to answer' line per pick, built from each set's three counter lines. In the fight, only your own strip chip names your twist ('1 · Boulder: Avalanche'). Nothing is drawn on the opponent.
ring.lock_in: Game 1: both players pick blind and lock at the same moment. In a set: the winner of the last game locks first, then the loser may change (the counter-pick, as fighting games give the loser). Both loadouts show on the versus card before the countdown. One loadout for all three lives; never mid-game.
ring.defaults: Classic (no picks) is every new player's loadout. The tree opens after the first ring win (the moment Basic controls unlock Wall and Heal), showing enhances and starter loadouts first; twists, sets and techniques open after the Full lessons. A player's first 5 Quick matches meet Classic or easy bots. Classic is held to the same balance gate as any loadout, so a player who wears nothing is never behind.
ring.starter_loadouts: Three per element, each exactly 10 points (validated), one click to wear, then any node can be swapped.
ring.balance_gate: Before a node enters ranked: the soak (tests/ring/test_ring_soak.gd, 16 pairings x 3 seeds) on starter loadouts, then on random legal loadouts. A node's win share must land at 0.47-0.53 against the same kit without it and against the other picks of its cost on the same key. Every loadout (the starters and the random legal ones) must land at 0.47-0.53 against Classic and against the others in the soak: a loadout is a sidegrade, never a power gain over wearing nothing. A node picked in more than 60% of its element's ranked loadouts, or with a win delta above 3%, gets its ring numbers retuned (never its identity). A node that fails two soaks leaves ranked (it stays in Practice and casual). Also before ranked: the true-string re-check (string_recheck), the recovery soak (recovery), and a soak metric for the share of each player's game spent shielded or unseen (inside his own Shell, Bubble, Dust Cloud, Blizzard, smoke or steam): no loadout above 20% (proposal).
ring.bots: Easy bots wear Classic; normal bots one starter loadout per element; hard bots all three, with a Beat rate from bend_ai.json. Before any set reaches ranked, bots must read the zones (step out of gas, seams and Blizzards; wash, blow or light gas; dry mud; jump crust and mounds) and cast the new skills they wear (Sulphur Vent, Mire, Dust Cloud, Blizzard, Cauterize; Shell and Bubble only if the owner brings them back, and then answer them too: wait them out or pop them). Bots read tags through the shared '+name' lookup, so a varied lead still matches bend_ai.json pct.strings.
ring.team_3v3: Same 10 points each. No limit on duplicate sets per side at first; add 'one of each set per side' only if the soak shows stacking. Team-only synergy nodes are greyed out in 1v1 queues so no point is wasted.
ring.fighting_styles: Open (question 15): this draft kept fighting styles and weapons outside the 10 points, but docs/fighting_styles_design.md says a ring loadout is style + weapon, both on the budget, each a branch of this tree. Until the owner rules: weapons stay out (on hold since 2026-10-08); a style's signature counts as its move-mode's one twist and its perfect-guard reward as that guard's technique; where a style lever and nodes touch the same number (the Defence lever and a guard node's beat, for one), their total change is clamped to 25%.
ring.online: Zones, terrain and reactions must be host-authoritative and synced; NetSession has nothing for bending zones yet.
ring.walls_note: None: only the WALL key's pieces count (round-2 spec 2.7). Mud Mound is low terrain under its own cap, and Ice Sheet hardens an ally's Ice Wall instead of making one.
ring.self_cover: A zone that covers its own caster (Shell, Bubble: both held) lasts no longer than its own lock, lets no lock start while it stands, and pops after 2 hits. Sight blockers are placed where you aim or left where a move ended, never centred on the caster (Dust Cloud is placed 2-6 m).

string_recheck.what: Every node that changes a true string's lead launch or a follow-up's lock or speed is re-checked against bend_ai.json pct.strings (Column then Pebbles at 0-30%, Geyser then Lash or Spear at 0-40%, Kick or High Kick then Punch at 0-40%, Embers then Punch at 0-30%, Pull then Palm at 0-40%, Gust then Slice at 0-40%, jab, jab, Pop) before ranked; the result is recorded here.
string_recheck.tool: round 3's lead_combos.py is not in this checkout or its history (it lived in the round-3 scratchpad): rebuild it, or measure with RingPredict through Practice's string counter, which uses the same functions the bots use

ring.recovery: No ring node changes anything you do off the deck (the Rise, the double jump, the air dodge, the Slam's self-lift, the edge) or lengthens an element's recovery reach (earth 11.3 m, water 11.8, fire 15.8, air 17.4). Key 3's travel moves start only on the deck (in the air key 3 is the air dodge), so their nodes are measured by the recovery soak instead. By this rule Hover and Lifting Down Gust stay out, Ride the Updraft became Peak Wind (no extra height), and Featherfall is open world only (the % ring has no Leap glide).
ring.classic_zones_ring: The tree's picks apply only under the % rules (RingRules.stock_on()). The classic Zones ring (Esc, Rules: Zones) plays Classic (no picks), because several trades exist only as % classes (rules.json stock.classes) that the Zones ring never reads.
ring.control_schemes: Keys, Basic (which plays the Keys routing: schemes.json controls) and the Wheel reach every node; the Wheel gains one entry for a worn new skill (earth and water 9 to 10, fire 9 to 10, air 8 to 9). First moves only and Direction reach only each key's first move, so under them the loadout screen greys out every node on a tap-twice move (the new skills, and nodes on Boulder, Column, Lift, Spear, Geyser, Surf, Lightning, High Kick, Jets, Breath, Wind Ball, Pull, Leap or Mend) with one line saying why.

help.name: The tree is the strip
help.what: The tree screen is the BendStrip on its side: seven chip columns (LMB JAB, E GUARD, 1 STRIKE, 2 PUSH, 3 DASH, 4 WALL, 5 HEAL) with each move's line growing up from its chip: enhances, the twist fork, the technique. Branches are coloured threads through the columns; the skill set is a band along the bottom that tints the chips it touches. Hover a chip and every node touching that move lights in order, each with its cost and its '+ / -' line.

help.name: Node cards
help.what: One help line of 64 characters or fewer, the trade chips straight from the node's data, old and new numbers side by side, and a 4 s looping preview recorded against the practice dummy (tools/bending/vfx_lineup.gd style).

help.name: Try it
help.what: Every node has Try: Practice opens wearing it (even unlearned) through MatchSetup.set_practice with a temporary loadout, the dummy set for it (throwing stones for Catch nodes, kicking floor waves for Mud and Frostwind, standing in a gas cloud for Flashfire). The open-world gate still applies outside Practice.

help.name: Starter loadouts and build paths
help.what: Three named starter loadouts per element, each shown as a route through the tree with a one-line plan; one click wears it.

help.name: Coach
help.what: After a match, at most three suggestions from your own tally only (casts per move, catches, perfect guards, falls by lane, reactions you caused), each with a why line: 'You held 80% of your casts and hit the Beat 1 in 4: Return to Sender pays for it.' '6 of your last 10 falls came off floor waves: Mud, Thick Wall or Frostwind.' It never equips anything. Rules as data (proposal: data/bending/coach.json).

help.name: Build for me / explain this loadout
help.what: One button fills a coherent 10-point loadout from your most-used moves; every pick gets one line, the whole loadout three ('Hold ground with Mire, push with Mudslide, mound up for cover').

help.name: Synergy threads and the team web
help.what: Worn nodes that combo draw a thread with its name ('Sulphur Vent + Flint Pebbles: your Pebbles light your own gas'); warnings too ('Forked Lightning: your puddles conduct his Lightning'). In a 3v3 lobby, before the match only, the team web lists what your three loadouts make together and the gaps ('No one can wash gas'), with the cheapest node that fills one.

help.name: Threat coverage
help.what: Five icons (along the floor, through the air, up from under, stone, lightning) show which threats your loadout answers, computed from the interactions table; with a known foe element one line more ('vs fire: Mud stops the Kick's wave; Frost Gust snuffs his Fire Wall').

help.name: Counter card
help.what: Before the countdown, both loadouts with one 'how to answer' line per pick, from each set's three counter lines and each node's answer line.

help.name: Path planner (open world)
help.what: Pick a node; the planner names the steps in words (the practice target, the teacher, the trial) as a journal line. No map markers.

help.name: Lessons
help.what: One Combo Lab card per world rule and per set ('Light the dummy's gas with Embers'), done by doing it, in the RingLessons pattern.

help.name: Loadout codes
help.what: Short codes to share a loadout.

help.name: In the fight: nothing new
help.what: The fight HUD gains nothing: your own strip chip names your twist and your own hands flash on the Beat. No markers, rings, frames, dots or highlights on anyone, and no 'combo ready' prompts. Reactions are announced only at the existing callout spot.

open_questions: The pairings: earth Sulphur (poison), water Mud, air Frostwind (ice), fire Magma, with lightning as fire's Storm branch rather than a second set. Is that the reading you meant? Frostwind now freezes the deck's grates as well as puddles, so it has water in every match; or should air make its own frost?

The loadout shape for skill sets: inside the 10 points or outside; one set per loadout or several; one set per element, or sets any element can carry (a water player wearing Sulphur); poison earth's alone? This draft's answers (one per element, one per loadout, 2 points inside the budget) are proposals.

The round-2 cuts. You cut the shell, the ramp, the bubble, the shards and the Lash jet on 2026-10-05, and you kept Breath with its smoke. Held until you answer: Shell, Ramp, Bubble, Jet, Shatter (the shards) and Clean Burn (Breath with no smoke). Bring any back as pre-match picks? Stream and Double Jab are left out, as the answers file records them standing; say so if you want them back too.

Twists held by the identity test: a volley in place of one move (Forked Fissure, Twin Geyser, Twin Wave, Twin Slice), a dash that hits (Surfacing Stomp, Breaker, Gust Step), and Reel (the Lash pulls him in and never KOs). Any of these as pre-match picks, or none?
Walls: only key 4 makes walls (round-2 spec 2.7). This draft keeps that (Mud Mound is low terrain; Ice Sheet hardens an ally's Ice Wall). Relax it for set terrain, or keep it?

New skills on the empty tap twice: Sulphur Vent, Mire, Dust Cloud, Blizzard, Cauterize (and Shell or Bubble if question 3 is yes). Yes, or twists only with no new moves? Air's key 5 stays empty: leave it, or Tornado or Cyclone later?
The Beat (let go within 0.2 s of the lock filling; a flash on your own hands) as the one timing rule techniques pay for. Yes? Without it, techniques need other triggers.

World rules act only on matter a pick makes, so Classic (no picks) plays exactly as today: Live Water became Forked Lightning's own rule, and wind moves gas, dust and snow but not today's steam or smoke. Agreed, or should some reactions be for everyone?
Forked Lightning makes a water player's own puddles a risk against fire. Fine, given water's current strength in the soak?

Sight blockers: Dust Cloud and Blizzard (placed, with a soak cap on time unseen) and Steamcraft add to the cover that already lets Breath's smoke stall a bot. Accept and teach the bots, or fewer sight zones?
Mud pools, Mud Mounds and frost crust stop floor waves and rolling stones: new counters to the Kick and the Boulder. The right amount of counterplay?
Budget: 10 points in the ring, and 6 growing to 20 in the open world. Smaller (fewer choices, easier) or larger?
Open-world PvP (co-op and PvPvE): when two players meet in the open world, open-world power (budget, ranks, practice lock times) or the ring's flat 10 points?
Should ring and PvP practice count toward open-world unlocks? This draft says no (cosmetic badges only).

Fighting styles and the tree: docs/fighting_styles_design.md puts style and weapon on the ring budget, each a branch of this tree; this draft kept them outside the 10 points. Which do you want? Weapons stay out while they are on hold. Until you rule: a style's signature counts as its move's twist, its perfect-guard reward as that guard's technique, and a 25% clamp where they touch the same number.
Should Fire Wall's own tick stop breaking a Lightning charge, like the new matter ticks? (Today it breaks it.)
Teachers and quest homes: may the Thủy Vân world session name and place them (sulphur springs, mud flats, a snow pass, a forge mountain, a storm watch)?
Visuals: use the converted Spellbreak effects as the look references, attribution kept, each checked by eye?

Player-facing words: Enhance, Twist, Technique, New skill, Passive, Synergy, Skill set. Plain enough? ('Variation' was the name of the round-2 layer you cut, and 'Mastery' is the practice tier the HUD shows, so this draft avoids both.)

build_order.what: Owner answers to the open questions; nothing is built before the pairings (1), the loadout shape (2), the round-2 cuts (3), the identity twists (4) and the styles conflict (15) are settled.

Data and loader only: read data/sway/skill_tree.json, validate it (extends_move and applies_to, costs, limits, excludes recomputed from changes[], starter loadouts, held nodes never worn), save a per-body loadout. Tests: the identity test per node, a % ring guard test per guard node (perfect, late and catch through RingRules.guard_outcome with the wearer's numbers, tapped and held), and the no-debuff contract (no node writes a victim's speed, aim, camera, lock or guard). On its own branch: several sessions share main.

The merge hook: a node's numbers merged over the bend spec in BendEffects.apply next to the existing grow merge; per-wearer copies of the stock guard and Patch numbers (guard_perfect_s, guard_catch_s, late_mult, return_mult, patch.lock_s) and of Bending.passive(), rules() and SwayCaster.modes_of() (the new modes and Cauterize only through per-body modes: air's key 5 is the same one-id patch key); variation tags with their stock.classes entries; one shared tag lookup that strips '+name' for every consumer (stale moves, stock.range.exempt, air_rules.lag_class, return_base_tag, the highlights, bend_ai.json pct.strings), with a test.
Enhances only, all four elements, plus starter loadouts made of enhances; soak, and the string re-check for the enhances on its list.
The loadout screen (the strip on its side), node cards, Try it, the versus-card loadout line, greying by control scheme.

Twists: first those on dormant specs that already dispatch (Hold the Storm's redirect_lightning, Ignite Step's burn line, Cleanse), then the new-code ones (Juggle, Avalanche, Rubble Wall, Whirl Turn, Pooling Wave, Splashdown, Blazing Fireball, Crescent Burn, Curved Curtain, Forked Lightning, Tailwind, Eye of the Gale, Rising Gust). Held twists only if the owner says yes. Soak.
New skills on the empty tap twice via per-body modes: Dust Cloud and Cauterize (Shell and Bubble only if question 3 is yes). Soak, with the shielded-or-unseen metric.

One skill set end to end, its visual gaps authored in the same step and judged by eye before the next: Sulphur first (the gas zone kind, the tick contract, Ignited Sulphur, Live Gas, bot answers, a Combo Lab card, the gas look with its outline and sound), then Magma (the seam), Mud (mud pools, the mound), Frostwind (the crust ridge, frozen grates, the Blizzard column cut to size). Soak each.
The Beat and the techniques (SwayCaster release window 0.2 s, own-hands flash, bend_ai beat_rate). Soak.
Synergy nodes, the Coach, Build for me, the team web, the path planner; the open-world gates (teachers, trials, ranks) when free_use goes off.
The remaining per-node visuals from the reviewed picks; BendLooks.warm_up must compile every new effect behind the loading screen.
